title: AKOM - Improvement of the well-being and quality of life of kidney tumor patients after standardized information on the importance of complementary medicine approaches
summary:
Background:
Many cancer patients use so-called complementary and alternative medicine (e.g., herbal remedies, nutrition, meditation) alongside conventional treatment . Although these approaches are widely used, there is often a lack of reliable information. Patients frequently rely on their own research or advice from friends and family and are often unaware of potential effects, risks, or interactions. At the same time, studies suggest that complementary approaches may improve well-being and quality of life. Therefore, there is a clear need for understandable, evidence-based information that can be easily integrated into routine clinical care.

Research Question / Objective:
This study investigates whether a short, standardized informational consultation about complementary therapies during hospitalization can help patients with renal cell carcinoma to become better informed, participate more actively in their treatment, and improve their well-being and quality of life.

Methodology:
This is a prospective, randomized study including 60 patients. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups:
Intervention group: receives a standardized informational consultation (approx. 30 minutes) on nutrition, herbal medicines, and dietary supplements
Control group: receives standard care without additional consultation
All participants complete questionnaires at several time points (before surgery, after surgery, and three months later). These assess well-being, knowledge, motivation, and dietary behavior. By comparing both groups, the study aims to determine whether the consultation has a measurable positive effect.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of kidney, except renal pelvis

interventions.name: Postoperative information on complementary medicine approaches
Control group: No postoperative information on complementary medicine approaches

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients who will undergo a partial or complete nephrectomy.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who do not wish to participate in the study.
Patients incapable of giving consent.
Patients who cannot undergo surgery.
Patients under 18 years of age.
